key_insight: CLIFE makes roadside VRU perception practical on edge devices by combining camera and LiDAR with online calibration and lightweight fusion. The key breakthrough is delivering robust multi-sensor detection and tracking without relying on cloud or server-grade hardware.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of reliably detecting vulnerable road users at intersections under occlusion, changing lighting, and adverse weather, while also meeting strict latency and compute limits for edge deployment.
method: Uses an edge-native camera-LiDAR fusion pipeline designed for real-world roadside intersections.
Performs targetless online calibration to align sensors without needing special calibration objects or manual setup.
Applies lightweight late-fusion tracking to maintain robustness while keeping inference efficient for edge computing.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CLIFE shows how to move multimodal perception from lab settings to deployable roadside systems. It highlights a practical path to robust sensing under real-world constraints without sacrificing latency or scalability.
visual_elements: System pipeline diagram showing camera input, LiDAR input, calibration, fusion, and tracking outputs
Intersection scene illustration with VRUs highlighted under occlusion and low-light conditions
Before/after comparison of cloud-based vs edge-native deployment architecture
Latency and accuracy tradeoff chart emphasizing edge suitability
paper_title: CLIFE: Camera-LiDAR Fusion Framework for Edge-Deployable Roadside VRU Perception
paper_authors: Tam Bang, Hoang H. Nguyen, Lei Cheng, Lihao Guo, Siyang Cao
